verdict.rationale: The only evidence is a passing mention that LangGraph's graph compilation 'provides a few basic checks on the structure of your graph (no orphaned nodes, etc.)' and lets you specify runtime args like checkpointers — a thin form of build-time structural validation, not a documented strict-typing/schema-validation system for catching agent mistakes. Missing for 10: documentation of typed State schemas (TypedDict/Pydantic) enforcing validation, explicit build-time error catching for agent-authored code, and any independent/hands-on confirmation that this validation reliably catches mistakes.
